findings.title: Same-URL subframes satisfy desktop IPC admission
findings.trigger: A subframe of the main webContents loads the allowed renderer URL and invokes desktop:v1:runtime-snapshot through preload.
findings.impact: admit compares webContents and URL but never requires event.senderFrame to equal the main frame. The new packaged test intentionally creates this exact subframe and expects request_denied, so the implemented boundary contradicts the required sender/frame admission. The handler also ignores extra IPC arguments, meaning malformed main-frame messages are accepted instead of rejected.
findings.correction: Require the exact main frame and reject unexpected arguments before returning a snapshot; retain negative tests for both conditions.

findings.title: Packaged crash test asserts the wrong runtime state
findings.trigger: The test kills the owned sidecar after a successful startup.
findings.impact: sidecar-supervisor.mjs:245-255 now returns disconnected and renderer.tsx:58-59 renders disconnected, while this packaged test polls and asserts unavailable. It will fail before verifying cleanup and relaunch on both operating systems, leaving the required packaged lifecycle gate unsatisfied.
findings.correction: Assert disconnected in both the bridge snapshot and UI, then complete the quit/restart and exact-child cleanup checks.

findings.title: Required packaged negative scenarios remain untested
findings.trigger: The current packaged script passes its listed scenarios after the frame and crash assertions are fixed.
findings.impact: It still does not inject startup failure, startup timeout, or service collision, and the only malformed payload is sent by a foreign window whose sender is rejected first. It has no preview surface to exercise preview isolation. The contract explicitly requires these packaged observations on each OS; listing the narrower scenarios cannot satisfy that gate.
findings.correction: Add native packaged failure fixtures for startup/timeout/collision and a trusted-main-frame malformed payload case; document preview isolation as inapplicable to this bootstrap only if the reviewed plan/contract accepts that narrower scope.
